beliefs: The box reverses the first whitespace-separated word, but drops its last character when the word has more than 4 characters [E1, E4, E7]
The box reverses the concatenation of all remaining words (joined without spaces) [E3, E5, E6]
Whitespace runs collapse to a single space and leading/trailing whitespace is stripped [E2, E3]
Empty or all-whitespace input maps to empty string [E1, E2]
Case and symbols are preserved within each reversed chunk [E1, E3, E4]
Punctuation attached to a word stays attached and is reversed with the word [E3, E4]
When there is only one word, output is just that word reversed with its last character dropped if longer than 4 [E1, E4, E7]
The exact truncation rule for the first word is uncertain: 'hello'->'oleh' drops one char, but 'there'->'reht' and 'world'->'dlrow' drop none?
